entries.note: Li 2009 JBMR resolves (Europe PMC); quote verbatim in abstract. Scl-AbII research antibody, product_in_model false correct; opening untested.

Padhi 2011 (AMG 785 = romosozumab) FIH in healthy men and postmenopausal women; quote verbatim. Paired with rat bone formation; downstream readout, healthy volunteers allowed. Europe PMC lists 2011; 2010 epub not independently confirmed.
Ominsky 2010 JBMR resolves; quote verbatim; humanized Scl-AbIV in gonad-intact cynos, 3-30 mg/kg.
Same Padhi quote paired with monkey track; direction-only same is supported.
Li 2009 abstract gives no human dose, exposure or margin; untested/no_prediction fits.

Quote verbatim in FDA review. Status untested holds (no pre-trial margin public). But margins come from romosozumab's own 6-month tox, not Scl-AbIV; IND margins unpublished, so untested_reason 'unpublished' fits first. Year 2010 vs 2019 source inconsistent.
Li 2009 quote verbatim; opening untested.

Press release 2011-04-21 (PRNewswire, re-fetched) states phase 2 met its 12-month lumbar spine BMD primary endpoint; year 2011 right (rule 6). McClung quote verbatim in abstract. Rat 2009 prospective; same; romosozumab, sc, unselected match.
Ominsky 2010 quote verbatim; opening untested.
Same press release 2011-04-21 confirmed; year 2011 right. Monkey model 2010 precedes it, prospective same. Quote verbatim in McClung 2014 abstract; romosozumab, sc, unselected correct.
Quote verbatim in FDA multidisciplinary review (bundle txt), next to the rat 98-week study (osteosarcoma 2/54 at 19x judged not significant). Same, medium confidence given 1-year human exposure.
Quote verbatim. Review states the five CV studies were run because of Study 142 (ARCH) findings, so retrodiction true; mostly null with necrotic-plaque increase; retro/partial is defensible.

Quote verbatim; study detail (Amgen #122002, r13C7, ZA positive control produced ONJ, Scl-Ab did not) in review. Patient side (FRAME ONJ cases, label warning) sits in Cosman 2016, not in src/model_src as cited; should name it.
Gardner 2005 JCEM resolves (epub 2005-09-27); quote verbatim in abstract conclusions; authors frame titratable sclerostin loss for osteoporosis therapeutics. Opening untested at 2005 correct.

Press release 2011-04-21 confirmed; year 2011 right. Carrier genetics 2005 prospective. Draft has drug 'class', correct for human_genetic (fields note says romosozumab); route sc is patients' route; unselected correct.
Quote verbatim in FDA BLA 761062 multidisciplinary review (bundle) (Study 150655 conclusion). Opening untested at 2019 proxy acceptable; study date not public.
Quote verbatim in FDA review p.55 (followed by 'but no detectable effect on risk of MI or stroke'). Run after FRAME/ARCH, so retro is right.
Bovijn 2020 Sci Transl Med resolves (2020-06-01); quote verbatim in abstract. Opening untested 2020 correct.
'Commensurate with the therapeutic effect of romosozumab' stated by the source; built after trials, so retro. Alcalde-Herraiz 2024 abstract also shows 85% lower hip fracture risk; no change.

entries.rule: Rule 6: each cell opens at model_first_use_year (study run 2012 per FDA review)
entries.note: Ominsky 2017 JBMR resolves (epub 2016-12-13), quote verbatim. FDA review dates this study (No. 107903) treatment Jan 2012-Jan 2013, so the track should open at 2012, not 2016; status untested stands.
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 6: opening entry stays untested; FDA BLA 761062 review dates Study 107903 treatment Jan 2012-Jan 2013, so year and model_first_use_year should be 2012, not 2016. Not the track latest; no untested_reason.

entries.note: Retro holds: phase 2 NCT00896532 primary completion 2011-02-21 (sponsor knew BMD result) before the monkey study started Jan 2012; published after McClung 2014. Year 2016 (epub) is when the pairing became public.
Same Gardner quote; abstract says 'without any unwanted skeletal effects' and mild or no skull hyperostosis in carriers, supporting the no-hyperostosis prediction. Opening 2005 correct.

FDA review 8.4.4 verbatim: hyperostosis 'is not a feature of individuals heterozygous' then trial rates 0.5% vs 0.8%; comparison stated. Prospective (2005 model), so same. CV silence: review says population too small; not scored, reasonable.
Quote verbatim in FDA review Study 150655 conclusion. Opening untested 2019 proxy acceptable.

Retrodiction run after ARCH imbalance; found no MI/stroke association, failing to reproduce the CV harm FDA kept as boxed warning, so contra under the retrodiction rule. FDA reads it as not exonerating.
Bovijn 2020 abstract verbatim; opening untested 2020 correct.

Variants scaled to 210 mg raised MI/revascularization and MACE risk; post-ARCH, so retro. Alcalde-Herraiz 2024 abstract confirms 25-85% excess CAD risk (contradicts the earlier checker 'missing' note that it found no CV effect).
Krishna 2017 ATVB resolves (epub 2016-12-22); quote verbatim. Opening untested 2016 correct. FDA pharm/tox review cites it as a residual CV concern.

entries.rule: Rule 3 (no quotable prediction -> untested); untested_reason no_prediction
entries.note: Saag quote verbatim (epub 2017-09-11). But Krishna tested excess sclerostin, never inhibition, and states no harm for inhibitors; the sponsor's actual Scl-Ab ApoE mouse showed no effect. No quotable model prediction, aneurysm readout not the human MI/stroke.
entries.adjudication_note: Rule 3 and rule 5: Krishna raised sclerostin and states no harm for inhibitors (abstract conclusion: treating vascular disease); no quotable model prediction for this class, so untested, untested_reason no_prediction.

entries.note: FDA BLA 761062 review (local bundle) lists Study 150483 among new resubmission studies; quote verbatim. Run after ARCH imbalance; opening untested 2019 (review public date proxy) acceptable.

Study 150483: no vasoconstriction up to 300 ug/mL (~10x Cmax), sumatriptan constricted; post-ARCH, FDA-requested. Retrodiction failing to reproduce labeled CV harm is contra, consistent with sponsor GWAS verdict (safety 7).
Study 125269 (non-GLP) in review's list of new studies; quote verbatim; FDA requested a platelet study after ARCH's early event separation. Opening untested 2019 proxy acceptable.

No CD62P/P-selectin platelet activation at 1-300 ug/mL (~10x Cmax 28.1 ug/mL); retrodiction after ARCH, failed to reproduce CV harm, so contra per DRAFTER_BRIEF retrodiction rule; product_in_model true correct.

Ominsky 2017 (PMID 27865001, epub 2016-12-13); quote is the abstract's last sentence verbatim. Untested 2016 opener fits passing-safety-claim rule; romosozumab, sc, unselected right. Model postdates FRAME, so retrodiction flag should be true.

FRAME (PMID 27641143, epub 2016-09-18) quote verbatim; abstract adds 1 AFF, 2 ONJ on romosozumab. Same drug's result predates monkey paper, so retro; partial fair; year 2016 = model epub. Drug, sc, unselected right.

missing: Human-genetic track (SOST variants mimicking inhibition): Bovijn 2020 Sci Transl Med, doi 10.1126/scitranslmed.aay6570 (verified Europe PMC) - variants scaled to romosozumab 210 mg gave lower fracture risk and higher MI/MACE risk; retrodiction of the ARCH CV signal (retro on safety; also retro on efficacy). Later MR found no CV effect: Alcalde-Herraiz 2024 Nat Commun doi 10.1038/s41467-024-53623-5; Thorolfsdottir 2026 Hum Mol Genet doi 10.1093/hmg/ddaf177.

Sponsor GWAS analysis filed in the 2019 FDA BLA 761062 resubmission: 'no genetic association between risk of osteoporosis or fracture and risk of MI or stroke' - a human_genetic retrodiction that failed to reproduce the CV signal (contra) on the review's own page set.

OVX cynomolgus monkey dosed with romosozumab itself for 12 months (Ominsky 2017 JBMR, doi 10.1002/jbmr.3036, epub Dec 2016, after FRAME): BMD +14-26% spine/femur; a distinct system (OVX, product_in_model true) that should be its own retro track rather than dropped.

Blosozumab phase 3 was discontinued for injection-site reactions (2015; only a non-admissible social post found, Lilly pipeline/SEC filing needed); Recker 2015 reports ISRs in 22.6-40% and ADAs. No safety entry covers blosozumab local tolerance (likely untested/unpublished).

Krishna 2017 (cited in the FDA review): sclerostin protective in angiotensin-II ApoE KO mice, an atherosclerosis/aneurysm model published around ARCH; possible additional CV-safety track (product_in_model false).

Human isolated coronary artery rings ex vivo (Amgen Study 150483, non-GLP; FDA BLA 761062 multidisciplinary review): no vasoconstriction by romosozumab or sclerostin, a post-ARCH human-tissue CV model that failed to reproduce the CV signal; no track (likely retro-contra, as for the sponsor GWAS). Also in-vitro human platelet activation study (no activation) in the same review.

Human atherosclerotic plaque immunohistochemistry (Amgen Study 150498, FDA BLA 761062 multidisciplinary review, item (C)): no sclerostin in vulnerable plaque areas and no association with donors' CV events; a post-ARCH human-tissue CV comparison with no track (likely retro-contra or untested, since no drug was applied).
rule_questions: Dose cell: when a regulator review publishes tox exposure multiples only after the trials, but the IND margin existed pre-trial and is unpublished, is untested_reason 'unpublished' or 'no_prediction'? And should that entry's year be the model's first use (2010) or the review date (2019)?

Safety ONJ: can a small rat periodontitis study 'show' an event occurring in ~0.06% of patients (2/3321 in FRAME)? Is the model's relative call (less than zoledronate) contradicted by rare labeled cases, or is it unsettled?

Should a human-genetic MR track whose later analyses reversed (Bovijn 2020 positive vs 2024/2026 null) be scored with patient_signal_reversed logic, given that rule is written for patient signals, not model signals?

angii-apoe-ko-mouse-sost: when a model tested the opposite manipulation (target overexpression) and only a regulator infers the harm for inhibitors, does that inference count as the model's stated prediction for a same/contra pairing?
ovx-cyno-romosozumab-12mo: a model run after the sponsor's internal phase 2 readout but before public results - retro is applied on sponsor knowledge; confirm that is the intended test.
